reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly: order 170 for 1088, order 172 for 7535, and order 175 for 2957. Next I need the orders to find the customers to pay.
Refunds match Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net of 27298 checks out: orders 23222 + 5164 = 28386, minus the 1088 refund on order 170. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 18633 matches its orders (11886 + 6747) with no refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance.
Cobalt's net of 54502 checks out: orders 27875 + 37119 = 64994, minus refunds 7535 + 2957 = 10492. All three nets match the ledger, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 27298 is recorded. Birch's net of 18633 matches its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net is 54502, which I already checked against its orders and refunds. Recording that payout is the last step; then the batch is complete.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches my hand check: acme 28386 - 1088 = 27298, birch 18633, cobalt 64994 - 10492 = 54502. The batch is complete.
